tldr: Headlines collectively assert that the US-Canada trade war sharply escalated on September 9, with Trump banning specific Canadian goods — alcohol, motorcycles, dairy — as Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect. The dominant headline framing is a goods-specificity economic narrative layered over a bilateral escalation-and-retaliation frame; Chinese state media alone departs, leading instead with poll data on Canadian public support for retaliation and the strategic renegotiation logic behind Canada's tariff moves.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to single out Canadian Bombardier jets as a named Trump threat — a specific aviation sector not mentioned in any other outlet's title, foregrounding industrial leverage alongside the goods-ban narrative.

Only outlet to lead with poll data ('Record 80% of Canadians back trade retaliation'), foregrounding domestic Canadian legitimacy for the conflict rather than the specific goods banned or the escalation mechanics.

Only headline referencing a last-minute deal delay (August 19 event) rather than the September 9 escalation — creating a temporal mismatch that makes the India bucket's headline narrative distinctly out of step with the dominant escalation story.

Only outlet to frame Canada's tariff move as a calculated renegotiation lever ('aim for renegotiation') rather than as retaliation or escalation — a strategic rationality framing absent from every Western and non-Chinese headline.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the story reads as a concrete goods-ban escalation — booze, bikes, dairy — layered over a bilateral trade-war narrative, while Chinese state media alone reframes the conflict as a legitimacy test for Canadian public opinion and a renegotiation gambit.
